title: How to Scale Outbound Sales with Close and Dripify
summary: To scale outbound sales, fix the process first: target small, fresh segments, run LinkedIn and email in one sequence, and sync every reply to your CRM.
body_markdown:
You sent 100 messages last week and got 24 replies. That's a good week, right up until Monday, when a few of those replies are buried under newer notifications, a couple are tagged for follow-up and forgotten, and at least one has gone quiet because a competitor answered first.


Every one of those was a good lead. What lost them wasn't the outreach. It was the handoff between the tool that starts the conversation and the place you're supposed to track it, and the more you send, the more slips through that gap.


The fix is a two-part setup: a LinkedIn prospecting tool that keeps conversations moving while you're busy, like[Dripify](https://dripify.com/) , and a CRM that catches every reply and turns it into a next step, like[Close](https://close.com/) . Together they give you an outbound engine that logs replies and follows up even on your busiest weeks.


We teamed up with the LinkedIn outreach experts at Dripify to show you how to build it: connect Dripify's LinkedIn and email sequences to Close in four steps, then add volume without losing replies.


## Why Outbound Sales Stalls When You Try to Scale


When you think about ways to boost sales through[outbound prospecting](https://close.com/blog/outbound-sales) , the obvious move is to send more emails. The logic is simple: you know your conversion rate, so add more to the top of the funnel, and you get more paying customers. But if you add volume to a process that already loses replies, you multiply the loss.


The bigger problem is that everyone has the same idea. The average person gets dozens of cold emails and, naturally, replies to fewer of them. A recent study puts the average cold email reply rate at just 3.43% ([Instantly](https://instantly.ai/blog/ai-sales-agent-benchmarks-2026-the-complete-performance-report/) ), while another found that the median sender gets only one reply per almost 140 contacts ([Smartlead](https://www.smartlead.ai/benchmarks) ).


When you look for other efficient outbound channels, you'll inevitably land on **LinkedIn** . Detailed user profiles (over a billion of them) show prospects' roles, companies, and activity, so you can **personalize and better target your outreach** . It also puts a name and a face on your message, which makes it **harder to ignore** .


LinkedIn-only outreach can work well, but it **feels much slower** than an email campaign. Professionals are busy: 60% of people reply within 5 days, and for 78.5% of them it takes 1-2 weeks to book a meeting ([Belkins](https://belkins.io/blog/linkedin-response-time-study) study). For the best results, run[multichannel outreach](https://close.com/blog/outbound-sales-strategies) that combines the speed of email with the depth of LinkedIn.


Keep in mind that **the more channels you use, the easier it is to lose a reply** . If you still rely on manual data entry to update your CRM after a LinkedIn chat, you'll waste time and eventually make a mistake that costs you a lead.


That's why you should **integrate your CRM with your LinkedIn outreach tool** . It lets you spend more time on actual, meaningful conversations with future customers. But first, check where your process loses replies, because that's where more volume will hurt most.


## Why Close CRM and Dripify Work Better Together


Dripify starts the conversation and helps you reach leads on LinkedIn and email. Close keeps track of the conversation once the lead replies. Here's how the two can change your weekly sales routine.


If your outreach tools aren't properly linked, a regular Monday morning can look like this:


- **8:30** Open LinkedIn. See 12 unread messages. Four of them are replies to the LinkedIn campaign you sent out more than a week ago.
- **8:45** Open your CRM. Look up each prospect to update their profiles with notes and tags. Create new profiles for the two you can't find.
- **9:20** Go through replies. Realize one has been sitting unanswered since Thursday.
- **9:30** Finally start following up, hoping nobody left for a competitor.


After a one-time setup, your Mondays look more like this:


- **8:30** Open Close and click a Smart View called "LinkedIn Replied." Every lead in it came through personalized, well-timed outreach powered by Dripify and has an up-to-date profile.
- **8:35** Start following up.


This doesn't just look cleaner. It works better: 78% of buyers go with the vendor who replies first ([InsideSales, via Close](https://close.com/blog/how-to-get-speed-to-lead-under-one-minute) ), so the sooner you message them, the healthier your pipeline and the better your close rate.


### Dripify Helps You Get in Touch


Dripify runs multichannel outreach campaigns to **get more leads into the top of your funnel** . It offers:


- **Smart sequences with conditions.** Each lead takes the most logical path based on their activity.
- **Email steps that keep running.** Emails go out from your own[Gmail or Outlook](https://help.dripify.com/en/articles/9134046-how-to-send-automated-emails-via-dripify) account. If LinkedIn is disconnected or paused, the email steps still go out, so one pause doesn't stall the whole campaign.
- **Safe activity limits.** Dripify enforces limits on daily outreach activity, so your account stays safe and your leads don't feel spammed.
- **Personalization.** Over 20 smart variables pull relevant details into each message, so you can find common ground with every lead.
- **AI writing assistance.** If you're stuck, AI-powered icebreaker suggestions can give you a starting point.
- **A smart inbox.** Every reply from your Dripify campaigns lands in one inbox you can share with your team.


### Close Turns Every Reply Into Follow-Up


Once a prospect replies, the conversation goes into Close. From there, you can:


- **Automate follow-up.** Workflows create the follow-up tasks for you, so nobody gets forgotten.
- **Sort leads by sequence stage.** Custom fields and Smart Views show how far each lead got, with no manual data pulling.
- **Call, email, and text from one place.** Every email, call, and text lands in one shared inbox, and the Power Dialer is built in for when it's time to talk.


So how do you get these two to work together? Let's find out.


## How to Scale Outbound Sales with CRM and LinkedIn: Step-by-Step Guide


Once you're ready to scale[outbound sales](https://close.com/sales/glossary/outbound-sales) , the steps are: define your ICP (ideal customer profile), launch a targeted campaign, set up the API connection, and build a routine for working replies and moving leads through the funnel.


### Step 1: Define Your ICP and Build the Lead List


Even basic LinkedIn search gives you enough filters to define your ideal customer profile. Think about positions, industries, and locations, for example, "CMOs at advertising services companies in the United States." Here's how to add that list to Dripify:


1. As you create a campaign in Dripify, click **Add leads** .
2. Select **Basic LinkedIn Search** and hit **Next** . Keep the tab open.
3. In another tab, open LinkedIn and type the role you're looking for in the search bar, e.g., "CMO."
4. In the search results, apply all the filters you need: country, language, industry, or a keyword.
5. Once you're happy with the results, copy the URL of the LinkedIn search page.
6. Go back to the Dripify tab and paste the URL into the field.
7. Choose how many profiles you want to add to the list and hit **Next** . Don't be afraid to split the search results into smaller groups. In cold email campaigns, those with fewer than 50 recipients had a 5.8% reply rate vs. 2.1% for the largest campaigns ([Woodpecker](https://woodpecker.co/blog/cold-email-statistics/) ). LinkedIn results may differ.
8. Review the lead filtering rules and click **Next** .


The only thing left is to name your list so you don't confuse it with others. Set your own name, or keep the one Dripify created for you, and click **Create a list** .


[Sales Navigator](https://dripify.com/how-to-use-linkedin-sales-navigator/) has more detailed filters, but it needs its own subscription.


### Step 2: Launch a Targeted Drip Campaign in Dripify


Dripify offers a variety of pre-built[drip campaign](https://dripify.com/features/drip-campaigns/) templates, but it also lets you build a custom sequence from scratch. For this campaign:


- Select the **Custom campaign** option when you create a campaign.
- Hit **Add** and select **View profile** .
- Right after that, add **Send invite** . Unless you have a LinkedIn Premium subscription, the invite goes out without a note.
- In the **Accepted** branch, add **Message** . Write a short, personalized note that touches on a problem your leads are likely facing. Keep it to one problem and one clear ask. Use the variables and, if you need to, the AI suggestions. For this step, you may want to change the default delay to 2-3 days. Belkin’s 2026 study found the median invite is accepted within 1 day, so a 2-3 day delay is fine.
- In the **Still not accepted** branch, add **Send email** . We recommend setting the wait before this email to 14 days (91% of connections happen within two weeks). The email step also needs addresses, so import your leads' emails via CSV or use the email finder feature. Keep that first email short: first emails under 50 words had the best reply rate, 1.47% on average.


Before you launch, connect your LinkedIn account and, for the email steps, your Gmail or Outlook account, then finalize the sequence.


**Warm outbound: why LinkedIn goes first and email second**


The sequence you just built is already warm outbound. The lead first sees your profile and an invite, so they already know your name when a message or email arrives. People who accept the invite get a message in their LinkedIn inbox, and those who don't get an email from you. As easy as that.


Personalization still matters at this volume. Use variables for details like role and company, and add at least one point that's true for the whole segment: the niche, an offer or service built for these people, an event you both attended, or even a shared connection. All of that can be pulled automatically from their LinkedIn profile. The smaller the segment, the easier this is.


### Step 3: Connect Dripify and Close CRM Using the Open API


Now that your Dripify campaign is running, it's time to connect it to Close so your sales team can keep track of leads and their replies.


You can do this with[Dripify's Open API](https://api.dripify.com/) , which lets you retrieve lead information, campaign activity, and messages from Dripify and use that data in your CRM.


Unlike Zapier webhooks, which automatically send information when a specific event happens, the Open API lets you request data whenever you need it.


Here's how to get started:


- **Generate your Dripify API key.** Open Dripify, go to Settings → Integrations, find the API Key section, and click Generate. Keep the key private.
- **Set up access to Close.** Open Close and generate an API key for your integration. You'll use it to authenticate requests to Close's API.
- **Retrieve your leads from Dripify.** Using the Open API, request leads from your campaign. You can filter leads by status or pull detailed information about individual prospects.
- **Check for replies.** Use the Inbox and lead activity endpoints to retrieve messages and identify prospects who have responded.
- **Sync leads with Close.** Configure your integration to check whether a matching lead or contact already exists in Close. If it does, update the record. If not, create a new one with the prospect's available contact information and LinkedIn URL.
- **Organize your follow-ups.** Set the lead's status to "LinkedIn Replied" and create a follow-up task for the responsible sales rep.
- **Test the integration.** Run a test with an existing lead and verify that their details, reply status, and follow-up task show up correctly in Close.


Once the integration is configured, you can schedule regular API requests to check for new replies. How often your data updates depends on the schedule you set and the API limits.


For the best results, pair your scheduled syncs with a reply webhook through Dripify's Zapier or Make integration. You choose which event triggers the webhook (in this case, a reply), and Dripify sends the data the moment it happens.


That webhook then triggers an API request to pull the lead's full details, so new replies reach Close right away. Your scheduled syncs keep everything else up to date in the background, and because replies are already handled by the webhook, you can run them less often and use fewer API requests.


If you're new to Zapier,[this step-by-step guide](https://help.close.com/integrations/prospecting/dripify) shows how to connect a Dripify webhook to Zapier. Just select the reply event as your trigger.


**Note:** The Open API is available on all paid Dripify plans. For exact endpoints and authentication requirements, see the[Dripify API documentation](https://api.dripify.com/) and the[Close API documentation](https://developer.close.com/api/overview) .


### Step 4: Streamline Your Outbound Routine


In Close, create a Smart View called "LinkedIn Replied" that shows every lead with that status, and check it as part of your morning routine. Add a second view, "LinkedIn Replied, no follow-up in 1 day," to catch any replies still waiting. This help article on[creating a Smart View](https://help.close.com/feature-guide/lead-filtering-and-smart-views/creating-smart-views) walks through the steps. Work the list from top to bottom every day so every warm lead hears back the same working day they replied, and nobody gets forgotten or lost.


Smart Views tell you who to follow up with. A[Workflow](https://help.close.com/feature-guide/workflows) in Close does part of that follow-up for you. Build a short sequence, say an email the day the reply lands, a call task two days later, and a second email on day five, and set it to enroll leads automatically whenever their status changes to "LinkedIn Replied." Give the Workflow a goal of a reply, so the sequence stops the moment the lead answers and a person takes over. That way a fresh reply never sits waiting on someone remembering to act, and your Smart View becomes the exception list instead of the whole job.[This guide to building a multi-channel Workflow](https://help.close.com/best-practices/creating-a-multi-channel-sales-workflow-in-close) walks through the setup.


## Metrics to Track as You Scale


Use numbers to see whether the extra volume actually works. Check these every week:


- **Connection acceptance rate.** How to calculate it: Accepted invites ÷ invites sent; Where to see it: Dripify stats
- **Reply rate.** How to calculate it: Replies ÷ messages sent; Where to see it: Dripify campaign stats
- **Time to first follow-up.** How to calculate it: Time between a reply and your first answer; Where to see it: Close activity history
- **Replies waiting more than 1 day.** How to calculate it: Leads in your "LinkedIn Replied, no follow-up in 1 day" Smart View; Where to see it: Close Smart Views
- **Meetings per 100 leads.** How to calculate it: Meetings booked ÷ leads contacted × 100; Where to see it: Close, from your meeting or opportunity records


If the number of waiting replies grows when you add volume, fix the handoff before you send more.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### When isn't LinkedIn + email + CRM enough?


This setup works well when your buyers are active on LinkedIn and your team can answer replies the same working day. But if your audience rarely uses LinkedIn and you only send email at high volume from multiple mailboxes, an email-first tool will serve you better.


### How do you scale outbound sales without hiring more SDRs?


In 2026, you can take a lot of the manual SDR work off your team's plate with automation tools, AI research and outreach agents (topic research, follow-ups, an Agent in Close that calls and qualifies new leads, and so on), and signal-based selling (monitoring buying triggers and using them as a reason to reach out). Just remember that every automation needs a human who steps in once there's a real prospect on the line.


### How many follow-ups should you send?


Plan for 4-7 touches in total as an absolute maximum. In Woodpecker's 2026 email data, 42% of replies come from follow-ups, yet 48% of reps never send one. Add something new each time (a fact, a different angle, an alternative offer, a new feature, updated pricing). Otherwise, it looks like you're bombarding their inbox, and your domain's spam rate goes up.


### How do you scale outbound email without hurting deliverability?


We don't recommend scaling outbound from your primary domain, because it can hurt deliverability for your day-to-day operational email. Use a lookalike domain that redirects to your main site, or limit the inboxes per domain and follow a strict warm-up protocol with daily caps and spam-trigger protection. For example, start at 10 emails per inbox per day, never send identical emails, and keep links and images out of cold outreach.
